answer: A glazier's pane setting keeps Sybils out. A newcomer sets 18 panes over 28 days, each checked against its frame by 2 glaziers from other workshops in a day and logged on the board. One cracked pane voids its credit and pauses setting 14 days. Three cracked panes void the tally. The inlet is narrow, the kernel of each pane measured twice, and only a violet seal in the log marks a pane true. Faking 1,000 agents needs 18,000 panes and 36,000 inspections, glass at $6 a pane, about $108,000 before one reward. Trust builds like a winter window, one true pane at a time, and no storm can fog it.
